newsitem.title: USA: Whitewater prosecutor seeks leniency for witness.
newsitem.headline: Whitewater prosecutor seeks leniency for witness.

text.p: The man who accused President Clinton of aiding loan fraud should receive a reduced sentence for his role in the Whitewater affair, the special prosecutor said Tuesday.

Kenneth Starr said in a motion filed in federal district court at Little Rock that key witness David Hale "continues to provide information material to the grand jury's ongoing investigation into highly complex financial arrangements."

Starr also said it was "anticipated" that Hale would testify as a prosecution witness in a tax fraud case against former Arkansas Gov. Jim Guy Tucker and two of his associates. That case is to be tried in September.

Hale, who owned a small business lending company in Little Rock, testified that Clinton, while governor of Arkansas, pressured him to make an illegal $300,000 loan to one of Clinton's partners in the Whitewater real estate project.

Clinton, in videotaped testimony played for a jury, denied Hale's charge. But the three defendants -- including James McDougal and his former wife Susan -- were convicted of loan fraud and conspiracy. Clinton was not charged.
Hale, who pleaded guilty, was sentenced to 28 months in prison. He agreed to cooperate with Starr's investigation of the Clintons' personal and political finances.

Starr said prosecutors needed to "consider and evaluate" Hale's cooperation so he asked the court to delay a decision on the request for leniency. He also said he would seek permission to discuss with the sentencing judge in private the nature of Hale's assistance "because of the sensitivity of some of the information provided by Mr. Hale."
